records.context: The guildmaster believes the strengthened guard should deter the bandits, apologizes for repeated trips and pays costs plus reward. System panels report77000 coins and a small share increase in Sao Jorge. Maria then asks the bandits' hideout location. Startled, the guildmaster asks her intent; she responds teasingly. Rumor places them in ruins deep in the Sahara, and he cautions against recklessness. Do not promise the bandits have already surrendered or identify a particular ruin not named here.

Tradition says only the greatest warrior, combining strength with a righteous heart and wisdom, can find it. He was convinced by her ghost-ship feat but admits asking any strong-looking person because the task is uncertain and nobody has succeeded. Maria dryly teases his permission to fail; he flusters and clarifies, and she agrees to try. He advances5000 coins, nonrefundable even on failure, then requests the map to the ancient city ruins and promises to accompany her, waiting at this town's gate. Keep the gentle humor, all amounts and uncertainty, not a guaranteed full reward or invented civilization/temple identity.

records.source_meaning: The villager is surprised the party knows of the monk.
records.whole_exchange_context: A villager recognizes the monk Maria asks about. The monk devoted himself to an ailing village; his medicine quickly eased the illness and prevented the village's annihilation. Maria wonders about medical knowledge, but the villager recalls alchemy and neutralizing mineral poison in drinking water. He shows the monk's book. Two clean source lines use actor2, Lil, including recognition of the book Charles mentioned; keep those source controls rather than silently changing them to Maria. Charles excitedly explains that rumored new experimental material brought him to the New World, that he traced the need for the alchemy book and is certain it clues a precious metal, but still needs its use. Maria postpones his rambling and asks the monk's whereabouts. The mood turns to grief: he fell ill from the same water, hid it and gave all his medicine to villagers, then died; the villager calls him God's messenger. He asks the party to take the book and continue the research by seeking its unseen ore somewhere in the world. Maria agrees. Keep the scientific details at the source's specificity, no invented lead, gold, contagion mechanism or order. Keep the source's religious praise, self-sacrifice and final loss without treating a rendering proof as medical or historical fact.

records.context: A villager recognizes the monk Maria asks about. The monk devoted himself to an ailing village; his medicine quickly eased the illness and prevented the village's annihilation. Maria wonders about medical knowledge, but the villager recalls alchemy and neutralizing mineral poison in drinking water. He shows the monk's book. Two clean source lines use actor2, Lil, including recognition of the book Charles mentioned; keep those source controls rather than silently changing them to Maria. Charles excitedly explains that rumored new experimental material brought him to the New World, that he traced the need for the alchemy book and is certain it clues a precious metal, but still needs its use. Maria postpones his rambling and asks the monk's whereabouts. The mood turns to grief: he fell ill from the same water, hid it and gave all his medicine to villagers, then died; the villager calls him God's messenger. He asks the party to take the book and continue the research by seeking its unseen ore somewhere in the world. Maria agrees. Keep the scientific details at the source's specificity, no invented lead, gold, contagion mechanism or order. Keep the source's religious praise, self-sacrifice and final loss without treating a rendering proof as medical or historical fact.
